title: Repair P04 onboarding, proof state and host safety
goal: Implement the IFX P04 acceptance plan in Guard, retain host and Target safety, and prepare a separately certified 1.2.2 release.
acceptanceCriteria: Expired proof produces a precise Host reason and recovery; failed Apply removes old UI success and step pass without writing a candidate.
Explicit proof renewal archives the old proof and requires a new Preview; exact expiry and changed bindings are fail closed under an injectable clock.
First onboarding presents step specific inputs and actual four root paths and outputs without requiring raw JSON or claiming protection.
A preflight entry captures independent baseline evidence before dotnet and installation, handles failures in finally, and rejects unsafe or ambiguous root topology.
Unrelated IDE processes do not block while Target writes are still detected and preserved.
The installed public Companion launcher starts with omitted port, alternate cwd and paths containing spaces.
Required Guard, Windows, package and PATH/Profile safety regressions pass before a new immutable patch release.
risks: A stale browser response could display success after a current Host refusal.
A preflight report that omits a safety comparison could falsely permit installation.
An isolated dotnet process could register a global tool in the User PATH if its guard variable is missing.
decisions: Reserve 1.2.2 and certify the exact release commit before publishing new immutable assets.
Renewal is an explicit human action and cannot change the independent external test baseline.
The Host remains authority for proof validity and all StateRoot writes.
IFX P03 remains failed; IFX adoption and human retesting require separate evidence.
validationCommands: Windows full and required CI at the frozen release source
